paragraphs_over6.paragraph: Contribution on model evaluation. We find a lower mean score with a favorable DM working-reference diagnostic alongside more breach occasions in the inspected FX record; this retrospective diagnostic is not selection-adjusted confirmation. Matched-history short-horizon QR changes mean pinball loss by (- )14.77%, with 376 rather than 360 breaches; its DM statistic is (- )5.866 and Holm (p=2.86e-7 ) (Tables 3 and 5). The distinct original FX primary has crossed elementary-score curves (Figure 3); the original Treasury primary is shown separately in Figure 4. Table 4 supplies an exact common-denominator bridge for the original primary, and Supplement S15 contrasts clean timing with deliberately illegal labels. CAViaR, Ehm and the endpoint-source studies already combine scoring and calibration, so joint reporting itself is not claimed as a new method (Table 1). The contribution is the decomposed, maturity-controlled evidence on this peak response and the limits it places on a single-score model-validation decision, not a systematic bias of proper pinball scoring.

The Treasury source is New York Fed Primary Dealer Statistics series PDPOSGS-B, Treasury-bill long positions less short positions. FR 2004A supplies Wednesday-close positions at market/fair value. Its instructions use trade-date accounting, with specified buyback treatment on settlement date, and include eligible forward and when-issued outright positions; the series is not settled cash holdings (Board of Governors, March 2013 and July 2024 instructions). The accepted snapshot has 706 seven-day-spaced records from 3 April 2013 through 7 October 2026, in USD millions. It aggregates reporting dealers and can reflect valuation or reporting-composition changes. Taking an absolute value after summing signed positions permits cross-dealer cancellation: a small aggregate can coexist with large individual magnitudes (Duffie et al., 2023). The absolute signed aggregate is not the sum of absolute dealer positions and does not identify gross exposures or pure customer order flow.

A forecast origin is the record at which the report is issued. Mature training outcomes are completed future-path labels available by the latest scheduled refit. Fixed-at-refit (frozen) F holds that label pool between refits; per-origin (rolling) F refreshes it at each forecast origin. Both update the observed current anchor. Historical peaks use their original recorded positions; translated increments shift historical signed paths to the current position. Headroom is the nonnegative excess above the observed floor, the absolute current position. These are forecasting definitions, not cash-resource allocations.

The neighbor menus are 180,360,720 at both FX windows, 20,40,52 at Treasury W52, and 40,80,160 at W260. The implementation uses exact order statistics and fails on an unavailable rank. For (k=52 ), ( (k+1) ,0.95 =51 ), while the ordinary .95 empirical pinball quantile has rank 50. At W720, W2880 and W260, however, W times .95 is integer: the lower ordinary rank and the adjacent corrected rank are both endpoints of the empirical pinball minimizer interval. The W52 distinction is specific to its noninteger probability-times-pool-size case. A later endpoint/rank ablation is retained in Supplement S5. Plain KNN at (k=W ) equals frozen F exactly; membership is then the complete training pool. Scaled KNN still changes responses at (k=W ). Long-window menus restrict neighborhood sizes below the full pool. Supplement S4 records numerical acceptance and failures.

The operational report L uses the same frozen completed-origin pool and refit times as F. Its endpoint sample is (|N_ i+H -N_i| ) and its one-based order rank is ( 39(W+1)/40 ). Add the resulting estimate to (B_t ). This empirical plug-in is distinct from the known population quantile in Proposition 2. Overlapping endpoint samples and dependent, changing series do not inherit the proposition's population coverage. Conditional coverage additionally requires the independence and symmetry premises and the correct endpoint quantile conditional on issue information. The bound supplies no pinball-loss ordering against F.

The H6 primary loss difference is negative in both issue-year groups: (- )12.012% over 6,262 origins in 2016 and (- )29.513% over the 363-origin partial 2017. The latter contains 5.48% of all forecast origins and contributes 8.64% of the H6 primary forecast-score reduction and 6.87% of the matched-history H6 forecast-score reduction. For both H6 comparisons, U and V fall in each issue-year group and on the fixed 947-origin grid. In contrast, H24 improves against its legacy reference by only 0.555% in 2016 and 33.007% in partial 2017; 70.83% of its summed forecast-score reduction comes from that short tail segment, and U increases in both groups and on the 265-origin grid. Supplement Figure S3 shows the issue-year contrasts. The fixed (H+1 ) grids retain favorable H6 original-primary and H24 legacy-reference loss differences of (- )16.388%/ (- )8.027%. These are decompositions and sensitivities of the same inspected record, not independent validation or a basis for retrospective forecast switching.

The original FX H6 primary and matched-history comparison have negative DM statistics, while the Treasury primary has a positive statistic (Table S6). The FX H24 legacy has DM (p=0.839 ) and HLN (p=0.839 ), so its 1.83% descriptive improvement is not statistically significant at the 5% working-reference level. At the declared bandwidth, 19 of 72 Holm-adjusted working-reference p values fall below 5%, compared with 18 at doubled bandwidth. The declared-bandwidth count includes 15 favorable and 4 adverse mean differences for the conditional method. The matched FX H6 comparison has Holm (p=2.86e-7 ); the Treasury primary has Holm (p=0.32 ) and does not meet that family-adjusted threshold. Its descriptive loss deterioration remains an adverse finding. On the Treasury primary grid, 7/40 strict breaches yield POF (p=0.00413 ) and CC (p=0.0157 ). These coverage diagnostics assess different nulls from paired equal predictive loss.

Within each source/H/W cell, the lower envelope is computed only over eight archived .95 reports: QR, KNN, scaled KNN, matched frozen F/S/K, AR and I. They share the completed-label history length and refit schedule, but this finite menu does not exhaust feasible reports. For example, C=B is feasible and has (V=0 ), making it a minimizer at (a=0 ) over all feasible reports; that floor-only action is absent from this eight-report menu. The reported endpoint winners therefore describe the menu, rather than all feasible decisions. Rolling and one-state reports are also excluded; the original cross-window primary references are separately labeled in Table S23. Supplement S6 retains all full and sparse-grid envelopes, endpoints and ties. Full-grid Treasury H6 W260 QR is never optimal among these eight reports, including both endpoints. At (a=.95 ) the menu minimizer changes on four of eight sparse grids: FX H24 W720, Treasury H6 W52/W260 and Treasury H24 W52. Treasury H24 grids contain only 12 origins. These are dependent within-archive sensitivities, rather than four independent replication outcomes.

Additional post-result / exploratory benchmarks sharpen this distinction. In the long-history short-horizon FX matched context, finite projected delayed ACI-style wrappers leave wrapped QR (ACI-QR) with 15.00% lower mean loss than wrapped F (ACI-F) while both observed breach frequencies are close to the nominal tail target. This is an empirical joint score--frequency result, not a conditional-coverage or canonical ACI guarantee. Headroom SAV does not beat matched F in either primary context. The fixed median improves on matched F and QR in the Treasury primary context, but its breach frequency still exceeds the nominal tail target; neither fixed combination beats QR in the FX primary context. For the original FX primary, observed mean loss favors QR in every training-defined position-change state; the evidence does not support an advantage confined to the high state or significance in every group. The original Treasury primary remains adverse across states. The lower target-level check retains the available comparison directions; the upper level remains unevaluable because of failed validation or insufficient tail information. Supplement S16 retains every menu, adverse cell, NA and working-reference diagnostic.

The executed QR specifications perform poorly on the weekly Treasury task. Their 25 level coordinates span the current observation through 24 weeks of history. The two hour coordinates, two weekday coordinates and gap indicator are exactly constant on this weekly source. Training-only centering makes those five columns exactly zero, so they provide no predictive variation and are not a demonstrated mechanism of overfitting. The original nominal design has 33 predictors plus an intercept, or 34 coefficients, with at most 28 varying columns and 29 potentially predictive coefficients before other collinearity, against (W=52 ) overlapping training labels in the shorter history. All four Treasury penalty selections are menu endpoints. Its 52 validation origins contain at most 3 disjoint H24 label paths, a path count rather than an effective-sample-size estimate. Correlated lag levels, overlapping labels, restricted tuning, target dynamics and reporting composition remain competing explanations. Neither the parsimonious sensitivity nor the aggregate panel separates those mechanisms.

A post-result / exploratory selected-fit readback examines the Treasury C2 menu boundary directly (Supplement S10). At ( =10 ), standardized response-normalized slope norms range from 0.001497 to 0.01937. Removing slopes while keeping each fitted intercept changes capacity by a mean absolute 136.8--832.3 source USD millions across the four cells. Relative to the lower empirical headroom-quantile report I, observed loss is 0.2432--2.192% lower; this descriptive difference has no dedicated selection-adjusted test. The fits have small normalized slopes and high headroom correlation with I, but are not identical to I or F. A boundary penalty and high capacity correlation do not by themselves show zero feature value. Three of the four C2 cells still have higher loss than F.

The expanded aggregate panel strengthens the negative transport finding but does not isolate its mechanism. Features and tuning menus, finite sample size, target behavior and reporting-regime changes can all matter. Downloaded cross-era histories are not original-release vintages; metadata/provenance for each key are retained. A prospective public-release protocol freezes the four procedures and selected historical-validation penalties before future issue artifacts. The first planned new release is after the protocol freeze, rather than retroactively labeling the already published October 14 observation as unseen. Because the release clock lags economic dates, the target includes prediction of unpublished measurements, with a nowcast/forecast mixture. A dated local amendment fixes future path values at their first actual capture and logs later revisions separately; operational capture and missing-week handling still require a bound adapter (Supplement S12). Results await prior timestamped report issuance and target publication; no live prospective validation is claimed.

before.abstract_text: Endpoint forecasts do not determine the maximum position reached along a financial path. We study the upper quantile of a sampled absolute net-position peak with a known current-position floor, explicitly matured training labels and matched-history controls. We state a pointwise floor projection, a classical absolute-displacement endpoint-to-peak bound and common-pool construction distances; none creates a new distribution-free coverage guarantee for fitted reports. Three findings delimit the empirical value. The original FX primary lowers mean loss by 12.660% on the previously inspected record. Its separately identified matched-history short-horizon regression lowers mean pinball loss by 14.77% but increases breaches from 360 to 376. Elementary-score curves for the distinct original FX primary cross, ruling out dominance for that pair. Horizon-specific short-history FX regression reports cross on 640/6625 origins despite ordered realized targets. The separately fitted Treasury regression primary raises loss by 50.79%, and the additional aggregate panel yields only 3/48 lower-loss original-regression cells. Exact gain decomposition, label-timing controls and additional mature benchmarks are post-result / exploratory, with mixed directions, failed fits and incomplete upper-target evidence retained. The Treasury exercise replays a downloaded vintage by economic date; compatible unseen-dealer and prospective public-release validation remain outstanding. The evidence supports joint validation of accuracy, calibration, report coherence and measurement compatibility, rather than a universal forecasting or funding advantage.

numeric_violations.sentence: Unlike the signed endpoint intervals of Wisniewski et al. (2020), the portfolio-loss maximum of Boudoukh et al. (2004) and the payment-deficit peak of van den Hoogen (2017), our target is the sampled absolute inventory peak

Related payment research studies maximum deficits, tail liquidity needs, and collateral requirements rather than this sampled absolute-inventory response (van den Hoogen(2017); Petrunia et al.(2019); Arjani et al.(2020))

Quantile regression targets an asymmetric loss, while conditional autoregressive quantile models and quantile forests provide established alternative conditioning structures (Koenker and Bassett(1978); Engle and Manganelli(2004); Meinshausen(2006))
The weekly application uses U.S. Primary Dealer Statistics published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York under FR 2004 reporting definitions (New York Fed(2026); Board of Governors(2013, 2024))

Additional benchmarks examine mean-filtered ordered historical paths, conditional quantile forests, and peak-tail estimation, with their full numerical and feasibility outcomes in the Supplement (Hull and White(1998); Barone-Adesi et al.(1999); McNeil(2000); Meinshausen(2006))

after.abstract_text: Risk limits on dealer inventories concern the largest exposure reached before a review horizon ends, rather than the position at its endpoint. We compare historical and conditional quantile forecasts of sampled absolute-position peaks for an FX market maker and weekly primary-dealer position aggregates. Simple historical rules prove difficult to beat. Long-history FX regression improves on a historical rule with the same history in both evaluated periods, and its later advantage survives a finite delayed coverage correction. Before correction, however, the regression breaches more frequently, while its ranking against a shorter-history rolling rule changes across periods. Weekly aggregate comparisons predominantly favor historical rules, including after stronger regularization. We formalize the known-floor target and apply a classical endpoint-to-peak bound under explicit assumptions. The results support joint validation of accuracy, breach behavior, and stability across reference rules, periods, and related series.
